brain.name: Brain
brain.desc: The control centre of the body. It handles thought, memory, feelings, movement and the senses, and keeps breathing and the heartbeat running on its own.
good: Regular exercise that raises your heart rate
Learning new things and spending time with people
bad: Head injuries – wear a helmet on bikes and motorbikes

eyes.name: Eyes
eyes.desc: The eyes focus light onto the retina, where light-sensing cells turn it into nerve signals. The brain joins the pictures from both eyes into one image with depth.
good: Screen breaks: every 20 minutes, look far away for 20 seconds
bad: Rubbing your eyes with unwashed hands

ears.name: Ears
ears.desc: The outer ear collects sound and leads it to the eardrum. Tiny bones pass the vibration to the inner ear, which turns it into nerve signals and also helps you keep your balance.
good: Keeping music and headphones at a moderate volume
Ear protection in very loud places
bad: Loud noise for a long time
Pushing cotton buds deep into the ear

nose.name: Nose
nose.desc: The nose warms, moistens and cleans the air you breathe, and its lining holds the cells that give you your sense of smell.
good: Breathing through the nose when you can
Washing hands often to avoid colds
Rinsing with salt water when blocked, if advised
bad: Very dry air for long periods
Picking the inside of the nose

tongue.name: Tongue
tongue.desc: A strong, flexible group of muscles. It moves food while you chew, helps you swallow and speak, and its taste buds sense sweet, salty, sour, bitter and umami.
good: Brushing or scraping the tongue gently

salivary.name: Salivary glands
salivary.desc: These glands make saliva, which wets food, starts breaking down starch and protects your teeth and mouth from germs.
bad: Some medicines that dry the mouth – ask a doctor if your mouth is often dry

pituitary.name: Pituitary gland
pituitary.desc: A small gland under the brain. Its hormones control growth, the thyroid, the adrenal glands, reproduction and the body's water balance.
good: Seeing a doctor about unusual headaches with eyesight changes

adrenals.name: Adrenal glands
adrenals.desc: Two small glands on top of the kidneys. They make adrenaline for sudden stress and cortisol, which helps control energy, blood sugar and blood pressure.
good: Ways to handle stress, like walking or breathing exercises

throat.name: Throat
throat.desc: The throat (pharynx) is a muscular tube behind the nose and mouth. It carries air to the voice box and food to the food pipe, and its tonsils help fight germs.
good: Resting your voice when the throat is sore

larynx.name: Voice box
larynx.desc: The larynx sits on top of the windpipe. Its vocal cords vibrate to make your voice, and the epiglottis closes it when you swallow so food goes the right way.
bad: Shouting or whispering for a long time

trachea.name: Windpipe
trachea.desc: The trachea carries air from the throat to the lungs. C-shaped rings of cartilage keep it open, and its lining sweeps dust and germs back up.
good: Covering your nose and mouth in dust or smoke

lungs.name: Lungs
lungs.desc: In the lungs, air reaches hundreds of millions of tiny sacs called alveoli. There, oxygen passes into the blood and carbon dioxide passes out.
good: Aerobic exercise like walking, cycling or swimming
Clean air at home and at work
Flu and pneumonia vaccines when advised

diaphragm.name: Diaphragm
diaphragm.desc: A dome-shaped muscle under the lungs. When it tightens and moves down, the chest gets bigger and air flows in. It is the main muscle you breathe with.
bad: Large meals right before lying down

heart.name: Heart
heart.desc: A muscular pump about the size of a fist. It beats around 100,000 times a day, sending blood through the lungs to pick up oxygen and then around the whole body.
good: About 150 minutes of brisk activity a week
Vegetables, fruit, whole grains and nuts
Keeping a healthy weight and managing stress
bad: High blood pressure and cholesterol left untreated

esophagus.name: Food pipe
esophagus.desc: The oesophagus is a muscular tube that pushes swallowed food and drink down to the stomach in waves, so you can swallow even upside down.
good: Staying upright for a while after meals

stomach.name: Stomach
stomach.desc: A stretchy, J-shaped bag. It churns food with acid and enzymes into a thick liquid, and the acid also kills many germs swallowed with food.
bad: Overusing painkillers like ibuprofen or aspirin
H. pylori infection from unclean food or water

liver.name: Liver
liver.desc: The largest organ inside the body. It cleans the blood, stores energy, makes proteins and produces bile to help digest fats.
bad: Too much sugar and fried food, which can cause fatty liver
Taking more paracetamol than the label says

gallbladder.name: Gallbladder
gallbladder.desc: A small pouch under the liver. It stores bile and squeezes it into the gut after a meal to help digest fat.
good: Losing weight slowly if you need to
bad: Crash diets and very fast weight loss
A diet very high in fat

pancreas.name: Pancreas
pancreas.desc: A gland behind the stomach with two jobs: it makes digestive juices, and it releases insulin and glucagon to keep blood sugar steady.
good: Whole grains and less added sugar
bad: Obesity, which raises the risk of type 2 diabetes

spleen.name: Spleen
spleen.desc: A soft organ under the left ribs. It filters the blood, removes old red blood cells and helps the immune system fight infections.
bad: Hard blows to the upper left belly
Infections that swell it, such as glandular fever

thymus.name: Thymus
thymus.desc: A gland behind the breastbone where white blood cells called T cells learn to fight germs. It is largest and busiest in children.

small_intestine.name: Small intestine
small_intestine.desc: A long, folded tube where most digestion happens. Tiny finger-like villi on its lining take nutrients from food into the blood.
good: Fibre from vegetables, fruit and grains
bad: Gluten, for people with coeliac disease

large_intestine.name: Large intestine
large_intestine.desc: It frames the small intestine, takes back water and salts, and forms waste. Trillions of helpful bacteria live here and make some vitamins.
bad: A diet high in red and processed meat

kidneys.name: Kidneys
kidneys.desc: Two bean-shaped filters against the back wall of the belly. They clean the blood, balance water and salts, help control blood pressure and make urine.
good: Keeping blood pressure and blood sugar in range
bad: Uncontrolled diabetes or high blood pressure

bladder.name: Bladder
bladder.desc: A stretchy muscular bag that stores urine from the kidneys until you are ready to empty it.
bad: Smoking, the main cause of bladder cancer
A lot of caffeine or alcohol

testes.name: Testes
testes.desc: Two glands in the scrotum. They make sperm and the hormone testosterone, which shapes male development.
good: Checking for lumps once a month
A healthy weight and regular exercise
bad: Long periods of heat, such as a laptop on the lap

prostate.name: Prostate
prostate.desc: A gland below the bladder that makes part of the fluid in semen. It surrounds the urethra, so changes in its size can affect passing urine.
good: Talking to a doctor about check-ups after 50

penis.name: Penis
penis.desc: The male external organ. The urethra runs through it and carries both urine and semen out of the body.
good: Seeing a doctor about pain, sores or discharge

uterus.name: Uterus
uterus.desc: A hollow, muscular organ where a baby grows during pregnancy. Its lining builds up and is shed each month during periods.
good: Seeing a doctor about very heavy or painful periods

ovaries.name: Ovaries
ovaries.desc: Two small glands next to the uterus. They hold the eggs and make the hormones oestrogen and progesterone.
good: Seeing a doctor about lasting pelvic pain or bloating
bad: Ignoring lasting belly or pelvic pain

fallopian_tubes.name: Fallopian tubes
fallopian_tubes.desc: Two thin tubes that carry an egg from the ovary to the uterus. Fertilisation usually happens here.
bad: Sexually transmitted infections such as chlamydia

vagina.name: Vagina
vagina.desc: A muscular canal that connects the uterus to the outside of the body. It cleans itself and keeps a slightly acidic balance that protects against germs.
good: Gentle washing of the outside with water

breasts.name: Breasts
breasts.desc: Made of glands, ducts and fat. After childbirth the glands make milk that flows through ducts to the nipple.
good: Knowing how your breasts normally look and feel
bad: Ignoring a new lump or skin change
